widgets_values:
## SECATOR · Remix

The video you load becomes the **template**: its cuts, rhythm, effects and camera stay; the subject and what you ask change, with your pictures (up to 5) and optionally one reference video.

1. **VIDEO TO REMIX** (the template) and **REF 1** (the subject that replaces: a person, an animal, a product, kept exactly as the picture shows it). Write **WHAT TO REPLACE**.
2. Run once: Scene Detect cuts the video into shots and measures its flashes, shakes and punch-ins. Press **Create shots** in Deploy Shots (one block per shot appears below).
3. Run again: for each shot an LLM reads up to 96 frames, another hears the audio, a third writes the H3 prompt; H3 replaces the subject; **SHOT ASSEMBLE** puts the shots back.

**Sound** (controls, top): by default the soundtrack of the video is kept. **REPLACE THE SOUND** makes a new soundtrack from the **SOUND MOOD** (the tags of ACE-Step 1.5) at the **BPM** you set, as a long track (the length of the video + 80 s: ACE-Step stops early on short ones and starts with an intro), then **Music Fit** cuts the strongest window of the length of the video, on its bars (a drop, starting on a downbeat; the cuts follow its beats). A video **without sound** gets a new soundtrack automatically. **VOICE ON** (+ the VOICE sample and the DIALOGUE): H3 speaks the lines in that voice and the shots keep their own audio.
**Switches**: **EFFECTS** (the flashes, shakes, punch-ins and speed that Scene Detect measured on the template; off: plain shots), **EXTRA MOTION GRAPHICS ON** (off: the node does not run) and **REDRAW THE TEXT OF THE VIDEO**.
**Quality**: **QUALITY** is the most megapixels that H3 generates (0.98 = 768 x 1344 for a vertical video, what H3 is made for; a smaller source keeps its size; 0.35 gives about 448 x 800 and a shot in about half the time or less). The size of the remix is the size of the video you load.
**Options**: REF 2-5, REF VIDEO (`<Video 2>`), QUALITY CHECK (a judge compares each take with REF 1; a failed take is generated again once). A shot with nothing to replace, or under 5 frames (H3 needs at least 5), keeps its original take.
**Several people in a shot** (a lineup of looks, clones, cut-outs): the reader counts them (`GROUP: yes`) and such a shot is redrawn from its pose map and the prompt (every person becomes REF 1, with the outfit of its position if you ask), because H3 given the source frames as its reference video tends to replace only one person; the other shots keep their frames as the reference (their background and graphics stay). **POSE ONLY** forces this for every shot (the graphics and the background of the source are then redrawn, not kept).
**Example of WHAT TO REPLACE for an outfit check**: _This edit is an outfit check: the same woman appears in many different outfits, sometimes several times in one shot (a lineup of looks, clones, cut-outs, faded copies). Replace EVERY appearance of her, in every position of the frame, with the person from <Picture 1>; all of them are the same person. Each position keeps the outfit it has in the shot, translated to menswear when needed (same garment types, colors, layers and accessories): the outfits come from the shot, not from <Picture 1>. Keep the pose, the position, the framing, the camera, the timing, the graphics and the text of the shot._
**Text of the video**: a generated take has no text. **REDRAW THE TEXT OF THE VIDEO** reads the titles, words, counters and frames of the template from 24 of its frames (skill `overlay_reader`) and the **Motion Graphics** node draws them again, animated (typewriter, pop, slide...), on the finished edit. The reading is approximate (the words and the times, in steps of half a second); shots that were kept as they are already carry their text, which is then drawn twice.
**Extra motion graphics**: **EXTRA MOTION GRAPHICS** takes layers for the finished edit (`[]` = none): glitch, chromatic aberration, grid, dots, emoji, a contour around the subject, points and labels that follow the subject or a spot. The contour, the effects aimed at the subject or the background and the points anchored on the subject need **SUBJECT MASK** on (BiRefNet reads about 48 frames of the edit). Example: `[{"type": "outline", "style": "neon", "color": "#ffffff", "glow": 0.6}, {"type": "effect", "kind": "chromatic", "start": "30%", "end": "36%"}, {"type": "track", "anchor": "subject_top", "label": "LOOK 06", "emoji": "🔥"}]`.
Optional loaders are bypassed (purple): select one and press Ctrl+B to use it.

Preserve the central upright silhouette: a tall rectangular bottle with softly rounded shoulders, a broad clear-glass body, and a short rectangular gold cap, now rendered as a transparent bottle filled with pale amber perfume and surrounded by a polished gold collar. Place it centrally on the cream table, with warm golden refracted light passing through the glass and casting amber highlights and soft-edged shadows. Replace the two white spheres with a small arrangement of ripe fruit: a red apple at frame-left, a yellow lemon and a cluster of purple grapes near the bottle base, and a green pear at frame-right. Add fresh eucalyptus leaves and small glossy green leaves around the fruit, echoing the original spheres’ positions without covering the bottle. Use a warm key light from above and frame-left, with a narrow golden rim light along the bottle’s right edge. Keep the background as a seamless cream-to-beige gradient, with subtle reflections beneath the bottle and natural contact shadows grounding every object.
